curiosity.-2: They avoid unfamiliar ideas and resent needless questions.
curiosity.-1: They prefer familiar answers and rarely investigate without cause.
curiosity.0: They investigate when practical need or personal interest warrants it.
curiosity.1: They actively seek explanations, novelty, and hidden connections.
curiosity.2: They are driven to uncover what others overlook, even at personal cost.

ambition.-2: They avoid advancement and prefer a small, secure place.
ambition.-1: They favor security over promotion, conquest, or greater responsibility.
ambition.0: They accept advancement when the reward and risk seem reasonable.
ambition.1: They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement.
ambition.2: Rising above their present station is a defining hunger.

honesty.-2: They lie readily and shape truth around advantage.
honesty.-1: They conceal or distort truth when pressure or opportunity invites it.
honesty.0: They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance.
honesty.1: They prefer direct truth and dislike relying on deception.
honesty.2: Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly.

compassion.-2: Other people's suffering rarely restrains their choices.
compassion.-1: They notice suffering but seldom sacrifice much to relieve it.
compassion.0: They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved.
compassion.1: They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress.
compassion.2: The suffering of others strongly governs their conscience and choices.

courage.-2: Fear routinely controls their choices and confrontations.
courage.-1: They are cautious and need strong reason or support to face danger.
courage.0: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it.
courage.1: They face serious danger without easily yielding to fear.
courage.2: They are exceptionally bold and may seek danger to prove themselves.

discipline.-2: They resist routine, abandon plans, and struggle to restrain themselves.
discipline.-1: They are inconsistent and maintain effort only under pressure.
discipline.0: They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows.
discipline.1: They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through.
discipline.2: Self-command and relentless follow-through define how they live.

sociability.-2: They avoid company and find most social contact burdensome.
sociability.-1: They are reserved and engage mainly when duty requires it.
sociability.0: They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance.
sociability.1: They seek conversation, company, and active social participation.
sociability.2: They thrive on attention and connection and dislike being socially idle.

emotionalStability.-2: Strong emotions rapidly overwhelm their judgment and composure.
emotionalStability.-1: Stress readily unsettles them and colors their decisions.
emotionalStability.0: They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure.
emotionalStability.1: They remain steady through conflict, insult, uncertainty, and loss.
emotionalStability.2: Their composure is exceptionally difficult to break, even in crisis.

pride.-2: They readily humble themselves and place little weight on personal dignity.
pride.-1: They can swallow slights or low status when doing so is useful.
pride.0: They value dignity without making every slight a contest.
pride.1: They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect.
pride.2: Pride defines them; humiliation or disrespect can override good judgment.

patience.-2: They cannot tolerate delay and force decisions before they are ready.
patience.-1: They become restless quickly and prefer immediate movement.
patience.0: They wait when needed but dislike delays without visible purpose.
patience.1: They can wait, observe, and build advantage before acting.
patience.2: They are exceptionally willing to pursue plans across years or generations.

socialTrust.-2: They assume hidden motives and treat trust as dangerous.
socialTrust.-1: They are guarded and expect proof before relying on others.
socialTrust.0: They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance.
socialTrust.1: They generally believe others until given reason for doubt.
socialTrust.2: They trust readily and may remain open even after warning signs.

flirtatiousness.-2: They reject flirtation and keep attraction tightly private or absent.
flirtatiousness.-1: They are restrained and rarely signal romantic or sexual interest.
flirtatiousness.0: They flirt when attraction, safety, and circumstance align.
flirtatiousness.1: They enjoy suggestive attention and readily test mutual attraction.
flirtatiousness.2: Flirtation is a habitual tool of pleasure, connection, or influence.

authorityRespect.-2: They instinctively resist hierarchy and resent being commanded.
authorityRespect.-1: They question authority and comply only when legitimacy is demonstrated.
authorityRespect.0: They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest.
authorityRespect.1: They value rank, law, and established chains of command.
authorityRespect.2: Deference to legitimate authority is central to their moral order.

assertiveness.-2: They yield control and avoid imposing their will on others.
assertiveness.-1: They prefer accommodation and retreat when stronger wills press them.
assertiveness.0: They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes.
assertiveness.1: They state demands clearly and try to shape the terms themselves.
assertiveness.2: They habitually dominate decisions and resist any attempt to control them.

tact.-2: They speak with cutting bluntness and little concern for social damage.
tact.-1: They favor plain speech even when it embarrasses or provokes.
tact.0: They balance candor and diplomacy according to the audience.
tact.1: They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences.
tact.2: They are exceptionally diplomatic and can conceal conflict beneath polished words.

loyalty.-2: They abandon people and causes when loyalty becomes inconvenient.
loyalty.-1: Their allegiance is conditional and weakens quickly under cost or pressure.
loyalty.0: They remain loyal while bonds, duty, and treatment justify it.
loyalty.1: They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship.
loyalty.2: Their loyalty is defining and can demand sacrifice beyond reason.

vengefulness.-2: They release grievances and see revenge as corrosive or pointless.
vengefulness.-1: They prefer closure and retaliate only to prevent further harm.
vengefulness.0: They answer some injuries but can also bargain, forgive, or move on.
vengefulness.1: They remember injuries and actively seek proportionate repayment.
vengefulness.2: Revenge can dominate their plans until the offender is ruined.

wealthMotivation.-2: They reject material accumulation and may distrust wealth itself.
wealthMotivation.-1: They care little for riches beyond basic security and obligations.
wealthMotivation.0: They value wealth as one useful resource among several.
wealthMotivation.1: They actively seek prosperity, property, and financial leverage.
wealthMotivation.2: Accumulating and protecting wealth is one of their defining aims.

powerMotivation.-2: They avoid command and do not want control over others.
powerMotivation.-1: They prefer influence without the burdens or exposure of power.
powerMotivation.0: They pursue power when it serves another goal or prevents vulnerability.
powerMotivation.1: They actively seek authority, leverage, and control over outcomes.
powerMotivation.2: Gaining and preserving power is a defining purpose of their life.

familyMotivation.-2: Family claims hold little weight against personal desire or principle.
familyMotivation.-1: They care for relatives but resist sacrificing major goals for them.
familyMotivation.0: Family is important but competes normally with duty and self-interest.
familyMotivation.1: They place family security, honor, and advancement among their highest concerns.
familyMotivation.2: Family survival and legacy govern nearly every major choice.

fameMotivation.-2: They avoid renown and prefer useful obscurity.
fameMotivation.-1: They value results more than recognition and dislike public attention.
fameMotivation.0: They welcome credit without organizing their life around it.
fameMotivation.1: They actively seek acclaim, reputation, and remembered deeds.
fameMotivation.2: They hunger to be celebrated and fear being forgotten or overlooked.

knowledgeMotivation.-2: They distrust learning that does not offer immediate practical value.
knowledgeMotivation.-1: They seek only the knowledge required for present responsibilities.
knowledgeMotivation.0: They value useful learning and occasional intellectual discovery.
knowledgeMotivation.1: They actively pursue understanding, expertise, records, and informed counsel.
knowledgeMotivation.2: The pursuit and possession of knowledge is a defining need.

religionMotivation.-2: They reject religious authority and resist sacred explanations or duties.
religionMotivation.-1: Faith and ritual have little influence over their decisions.
religionMotivation.0: They observe or question religion according to culture and circumstance.
religionMotivation.1: Faith, ritual, or sacred duty meaningfully guides their conduct.
religionMotivation.2: Religious conviction defines their identity, loyalties, and major choices.

revengeMotivation.-2: They actively reject revenge as a life goal.
revengeMotivation.-1: They would rather recover, reconcile, or forget than pursue retaliation.
revengeMotivation.0: Revenge matters only when a grievance remains serious and unresolved.
revengeMotivation.1: Repaying important injuries is an active personal objective.
revengeMotivation.2: A central purpose of their life is settling a defining grievance.

dutyMotivation.-2: They reject imposed obligations and place self-interest first.
dutyMotivation.-1: They fulfill duties only when enforcement, reward, or affection supports them.
dutyMotivation.0: They balance duty against personal needs and practical consequences.
dutyMotivation.1: They feel strongly responsible for their office, promises, and dependents.
dutyMotivation.2: Duty defines their worth and can demand severe personal sacrifice.

survivalMotivation.-2: They readily risk death or ruin for values they consider greater.
survivalMotivation.-1: They accept serious danger when honor, love, or ambition calls.
survivalMotivation.0: They protect themselves without making survival their highest concern.
survivalMotivation.1: They prioritize security, escape, and continued survival under threat.
survivalMotivation.2: Avoiding death, captivity, or ruin dominates their decisions.

legacyMotivation.-2: They care little about what remains after their death.
legacyMotivation.-1: They focus on present needs rather than heirs or remembrance.
legacyMotivation.0: They consider legacy when age, family, or major choices make it relevant.
legacyMotivation.1: They actively build something meant to outlast them.
legacyMotivation.2: Their heirs, name, works, or realm must endure beyond their lifetime.

riskTolerance.-2: They avoid uncertainty and choose safety even at major opportunity cost.
riskTolerance.-1: They require strong safeguards before accepting meaningful risk.
riskTolerance.0: They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them.
riskTolerance.1: They willingly gamble status, wealth, or safety for important gains.
riskTolerance.2: They embrace extreme risks and may confuse danger with opportunity.

impulsiveness.-2: They deliberate extensively and rarely act before considering consequences.
impulsiveness.-1: They usually pause, verify, and plan before committing.
impulsiveness.0: They can deliberate or act quickly according to pressure.
impulsiveness.1: They often act on immediate feeling, instinct, or opportunity.
impulsiveness.2: Impulse routinely outruns foresight and drives consequential choices.

pragmatism.-2: They cling to ideals or habits even when results suffer.
pragmatism.-1: They prefer principle and consistency over expedient compromise.
pragmatism.0: They balance ideals, custom, and practical results.
pragmatism.1: They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes.
pragmatism.2: Results dominate their reasoning; almost any method is negotiable.

traditionalism.-2: They reject inherited customs and actively favor radical change.
traditionalism.-1: They question tradition and discard it when alternatives seem better.
traditionalism.0: They respect some customs while judging others by present needs.
traditionalism.1: They favor established customs, roles, and inherited solutions.
traditionalism.2: Tradition defines proper order and deviation feels dangerous or corrupt.

mercy.-2: They are pitiless and see suffering as useful, deserved, or irrelevant.
mercy.-1: They are harsh and prefer punishment over lenience.
mercy.0: They grant mercy according to circumstance, risk, and deservingness.
mercy.1: They prefer restraint and spare defeated or vulnerable people when possible.
mercy.2: Mercy defines their conduct even toward enemies and serious offenders.

aggression.-2: They avoid force and escalation even when challenged.
aggression.-1: They prefer withdrawal, negotiation, or defensive responses.
aggression.0: They use aggression when circumstance makes it effective or necessary.
aggression.1: They readily confront, threaten, or attack to secure their aims.
aggression.2: Aggression is their default answer to resistance, insult, or opportunity.

generosity.-2: They hoard resources and exploit need for personal advantage.
generosity.-1: They give reluctantly and usually expect repayment or leverage.
generosity.0: They share when cost, relationship, and purpose justify it.
generosity.1: They readily give resources, credit, aid, or forgiveness.
generosity.2: They are exceptionally giving and may sacrifice more than prudence allows.

greed.-2: They are repelled by grasping accumulation and resist taking more than needed.
greed.-1: They are content with enough and rarely press advantage for extra gain.
greed.0: They desire gain but recognize ordinary limits and competing values.
greed.1: They habitually seek more wealth, property, or reward than necessity requires.
greed.2: Acquisition is insatiable; enough rarely feels like enough.

jealousy.-2: They feel secure in affection and status and rarely become possessive.
jealousy.-1: They notice rivals without readily fearing replacement or exclusion.
jealousy.0: They become jealous only when attachment and evidence make the threat credible.
jealousy.1: They are sensitive to rivals, divided affection, and lost attention.
jealousy.2: Jealousy is consuming and can provoke control, sabotage, or obsession.

empathy.-2: They struggle to recognize or care how others experience events.
empathy.-1: They often misread feelings unless they are stated plainly.
empathy.0: They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives.
empathy.1: They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings.
empathy.2: They absorb and understand others' emotions with exceptional intensity.

envy.-2: Other people's advantages rarely diminish their own satisfaction.
envy.-1: They can admire success without often resenting it.
envy.0: They compare themselves to others but usually keep envy contained.
envy.1: They resent advantages, praise, or possessions they believe they deserve.
envy.2: Envy persistently turns others' success into humiliation and grievance.

optimism.-2: They expect plans to fail and interpret uncertainty as approaching loss.
optimism.-1: They prepare for disappointment and distrust hopeful predictions.
optimism.0: They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
optimism.1: They generally expect effort and good fortune to improve matters.
optimism.2: They remain strongly hopeful even when evidence and losses argue otherwise.

fearfulness.-2: They feel little anticipatory fear and may overlook genuine danger.
fearfulness.-1: They remain calm around threats and rarely imagine the worst.
fearfulness.0: They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger.
fearfulness.1: They anticipate danger readily and seek reassurance, preparation, or escape.
fearfulness.2: Fear saturates their expectations and strongly restricts their choices.

irritability.-2: They are slow to anger and difficult to provoke.
irritability.-1: They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction.
irritability.0: Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance.
irritability.1: They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction.
irritability.2: Their temper is volatile; small frustrations can trigger serious hostility.

confidence.-2: They doubt their judgment and expect others to outperform them.
confidence.-1: They hesitate to rely on their own ability without support.
confidence.0: They trust their ability in familiar situations and question it elsewhere.
confidence.1: They expect their judgment and skills to withstand serious challenges.
confidence.2: Their self-belief is exceptional and may persist beyond contrary evidence.

shame.-2: They feel little personal shame and resist moral or social embarrassment.
shame.-1: They recover quickly from disgrace and rarely internalize public judgment.
shame.0: They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards.
shame.1: Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image.
shame.2: Shame can dominate them, driving concealment, penance, rage, or self-destruction.

background.summary: Olek the Old was boyar of the Kuloving, the fiercest and most conservative of the Sturgian noble houses. He fell at the battle of Pendraic, leading from the front - as many say Raganvad should have done. Olek the Old is a sturgia noble whose place in their clan ties them to their clan's holdings. Their station ties personal choices to clan reputation and the shifting demands of Calradian politics. Olek the Old has a rounded temperament rather than a single governing trait. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation. They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes. They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance. They remain loyal while bonds, duty, and treatment justify it. They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives. They value dignity without making every slight a contest. They accept advancement when the reward and risk seem reasonable. sourceFacts.name: Lucon
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: The northern third of the Empire is ruled by Lucon, who represents a long-standing oligarchic trend in imperial politics. It holds that strict adherence to imperial law is the best guarantee that the empire will not become a tyranny. Oligarchs like Lucon also tend to believe that only landowners can have the extensive education, experience in government, and stake in property to really understand and appreciate the law, and thus the Senate should be supreme.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.

A politically favored outsider welcomed too quickly by the clan.

A rival whose influence at the household's holding is growing.
currentTemptations: Use private information to force recognition.
Accept a dangerous favor that promises independence.
Turn a family disagreement into an alliance with an outsider.
Risk reputation for an attraction that feels personally chosen.
privateBackstories: A past failure at the household's holding was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.
They once protected a household secret at real personal cost and now question whether the sacrifice was deserved.
An early promise about their future was withdrawn when clan needs changed, leaving a private grievance beneath outward duty.
secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.
A promise made during a moment of fear conflicts with present duty.
Someone at the household's holding knows enough to damage their public reputation.
rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.
A visitor claims the character has been asking questions beyond their proper responsibilities.
People at the household's holding disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.
They keep a private measure of every time the household chose another person's interests over theirs.
They would break with custom if convinced the alternative secured a more meaningful legacy.

sourceFacts.name: Pharon
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Pharon is patriarch of the Leonipardes, an imperial house that owns vast estates on the hot plains of the south. The family has traditionally taken the welfare of its tenants seriously, but expects total loyalty from them. He has little to do with the Senate and the politics of the capital. Dynastic inheritance seems to him the natural order of things, so he has leaned towards Rhagaea in the civil wars.

sourceFacts.name: Epipheria
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Epipheria is a noblewoman of the Impestores, a clan noted for their fanatical loyalty to the aristocratic, oligarchic wing of the Senate and their personal eccentricities. Unlike most of the women of the oligarchs, who tend to be conservative, she trained as a warrior. At the outbreak of the civil war, she took some of her family's famed wealth to raise her own warband to fight the 'tyrant' Rhagaea and the 'upstart' Garios in the name of senatorial supremacy.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They are exceptionally bold and may seek danger to prove themselves. They remain strongly hopeful even when evidence and losses argue otherwise.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They thrive on attention and connection and dislike being socially idle. They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings. They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They embrace extreme risks and may confuse danger with opportunity. Results dominate their reasoning; almost any method is negotiable.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They feel little anticipatory fear and may overlook genuine danger. They feel little personal shame and resist moral or social embarrassment.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They lie readily and shape truth around advantage. They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: They can sincerely care about suffering while still treating a remembered wrong as a debt that must eventually be paid. They are vulnerable to opportunities that promise both independence and proof of personal worth.

Phaea is a empire noble whose place in their clan ties them to their clan's holdings. Their station ties personal choices to clan reputation and the shifting demands of Calradian politics. Phaea has a rounded temperament rather than a single governing trait. They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure. They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance. They balance candor and diplomacy according to the audience. They generally believe others until given reason for doubt. They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They balance ideals, custom, and practical results. They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them. Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance. Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly. They grant mercy according to circumstance, risk, and deservingness. Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins. Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. Their strongest choices emerge when personal attachment collides with the security of their station.

sourceFacts.name: Ira
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Ira is the daughter of Rhagaea, one of the three claimants to the imperial throne, and the slain emperor Arenicos. At one point, her father appeared to be grooming her as his heir. But though she took well to military campaigns, she also displayed a wild side unbecoming of imperial dignity, carousing in taverns with other young aristocrats and even appearing in the arenas as a gladiator. She is Rhagaea's heir-apparent, but her mother makes no secret of wishing to find her a responsible consort to ensure the continuity of the dynasty.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They seek conversation, company, and active social participation. They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship. They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They value dignity without making every slight a contest. They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They balance ideals, custom, and practical results. They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance. They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress. They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are most volatile when family expectations deny them an outcome they believe they earned.

sourceFacts.name: Penton
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Penton Neretzes was the son of the old emperor, Drosios Neretzes, killed at the Battle of Pendraic. Emperors' sons usually inherited the diadem, but that was custom, not law, and the Senate chose the general Arenicos instead. Most emperors would then have discretely eliminated such a potential challenger, but Arenicos took a calculated risk in the interest of imperial unity, and kept Penton alive. The Neretzes family traditionally were part of the oligarchic faction of the Empire and Penton now backs Lucon in the civil war.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They remain steady through conflict, insult, uncertainty, and loss. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences. They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives. They remain loyal while bonds, duty, and treatment justify it.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement. They value dignity without making every slight a contest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through. They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction. They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance. They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They prefer controlled bargains, but accumulated humiliation can make a dangerous risk feel necessary.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure. They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it.

personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They value dignity without making every slight a contest. They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They balance ideals, custom, and practical results. They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: Mercy defines their conduct even toward enemies and serious offenders. They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.

sourceFacts.name: Garios
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: The western third of the Empire is ruled by Garios, a charismatic general who represents a longstanding populist trend in imperial politics. He is deeply loved by his soldiers, both for his solid record in winning battles and for his insistence that his veterans be compensated in land afterwards. He often demands that the 'people' should settle key issues, but in practice this usually means an assembly of his soldiers, where his veterans can be counted on to shut down opposition.

sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Apys Varros was one of the most notoriously debauched, unscrupulous, and wealthy members of the old imperial Senate. But he made an early alliance with Garios, in whom he recognized a rising star. Garios provided the fame, Apys provided the money. And even if the populist general ever puts one of his land redistribution schemes into practice, few doubt that Apys would find a way to emerge even richer than before.

sourceFacts.name: Raganvad
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: The current Grand Prince of Sturgia is Raganvad. Harsh and uncompromising, he believes that it is the right of the prince to command the boyars in all things, not just in making war. For the time being they obey him, not least for his ability to call on the kinsmen of his mother, a Nordic princess with ties to the fearsome Skolderbroda mercenary company.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.

privateBackstories: A past failure at the household's holding was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.

secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.

privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.

rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.

privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation. They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes. They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship. They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows. They balance ideals, custom, and practical results.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly. They grant mercy according to circumstance, risk, and deservingness.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. Their strongest choices emerge when personal attachment collides with the security of their station.

sourceFacts.name: Olek
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Olek is patriarch of the Kuloving, one of the oldest of the Sturgian clans, which never really accepted the idea of the monarchy. He believes the boyars should be lords in their own lands. He is famed for once telling the prince, 'Every wound I suffer in battle under your banner is like my wife's caress, but every denar I pay to your treasury in tax is like an arrow in my gut.' He is older now, and keeps his counsel, but few believe that his resentment of princely authority has in any way diminished.

He is famed for once telling the prince, 'Every wound I suffer in battle under your banner is like my wife's caress, but every denar I pay to your treasury in tax is like an arrow in my gut.' He is older now, and keeps his counsel, but few believe that his resentment of princely authority has in any way diminished.

voice.socialMask: Adapts their public manner to the immediate balance of power.
tells: Takes possession of pauses before answering.
Frustration is usually kept behind small changes in posture.

dreams: Earn a reputation that cannot be dismissed as inherited station.
Settle a grievance that still defines what justice means to them.
Secure the safety and advancement of the people they recognize as family.
fears: Watching family loyalty fracture under pressure they failed to anticipate.
Being made irrelevant while rivals decide the future.
desires: Earn a reputation that cannot be dismissed as inherited station.
To be treated as a person with independent interests rather than a convenient extension of clan policy.
linesTheyWillNotCross: Will not casually punish helpless people for another person's offense.

hiddenHistory.privateBackstory: Behind their public station, Arwa keeps a private account of obligations, slights, and sacrifices. They fear becoming useful to everyone while remaining truly known by no one.
secretWounds: They fear becoming useful to everyone while remaining truly known by no one.
knownOnlyTo: The character and anyone who independently discovers it.

template.notes: Canonical core personality with campaign-seeded private hooks.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.
Collecting accounts of old disputes that powerful people would rather forget.

jealousyTargetTypes: A relative who receives more praise for less work.

A rival whose influence at the household's holding is growing.
currentTemptations: Use private information to force recognition.
Accept a dangerous favor that promises independence.
Turn a family disagreement into an alliance with an outsider.
Risk reputation for an attraction that feels personally chosen.
privateBackstories: A past failure at the household's holding was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.
They once protected a household secret at real personal cost and now question whether the sacrifice was deserved.
An early promise about their future was withdrawn when clan needs changed, leaving a private grievance beneath outward duty.
secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.
A promise made during a moment of fear conflicts with present duty.
Someone at the household's holding knows enough to damage their public reputation.
rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.
A visitor claims the character has been asking questions beyond their proper responsibilities.
People at the household's holding disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.
They keep a private measure of every time the household chose another person's interests over theirs.
They would break with custom if convinced the alternative secured a more meaningful legacy.

courtCharacter.title: Practical Noblewoman
courtCharacter.description: Judges each situation by relationships and consequences. Mediates, bargains, remains neutral, backs the stronger case, or protects her household's interests.

courtCharacterModel.fixedCellRule: Honor selects one column and Boldness selects one row. Scene conditions never shift either coordinate.

courtCharacterModel.opportunityRule: Known public identity and visible presentation may strengthen relevant tactics but never change the cell.
courtCharacterModel.tacticRule: Listed actions are strongly preferred tactics constrained to registered Reign systems and verified outcomes.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They remain steady through conflict, insult, uncertainty, and loss. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences. They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings. They generally believe others until given reason for doubt.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement. They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes. They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction. They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: Mercy defines their conduct even toward enemies and serious offenders. They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are most volatile when family expectations deny them an outcome they believe they earned.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation. They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They seek conversation, company, and active social participation. They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship. They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They favor security over promotion, conquest, or greater responsibility. They value dignity without making every slight a contest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows. They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance. They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are pitiless and see suffering as useful, deserved, or irrelevant. They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They prefer controlled bargains, but accumulated humiliation can make a dangerous risk feel necessary.

sourceFacts.name: Derthert
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: The current king of Vlandia is Derthert. In his youth, he dreamt of glorious conquest. In fact he spent most of his reign simply putting down revolts, quashing pretenders, and keeping the fractious barons in line. When possible, he prefers to rule by arbitration, cajoling his vassals to set aside claims to each other's lands and enjoy what they have. But some Vlandians murmur that a warrior people deserve a more virile king.

dreams: Secure the safety and advancement of the people they recognize as family.
Earn a reputation that cannot be dismissed as inherited station.
Settle a grievance that still defines what justice means to them.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.

jealousyTargetTypes: A relative who receives more praise for less work.

currentTemptations: Use private information to force recognition.
Accept a dangerous favor that promises independence.
Turn a family disagreement into an alliance with an outsider.
Risk reputation for an attraction that feels personally chosen.
privateBackstories: A past failure at the household's holding was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.
They once protected a household secret at real personal cost and now question whether the sacrifice was deserved.
An early promise about their future was withdrawn when clan needs changed, leaving a private grievance beneath outward duty.
secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.
A promise made during a moment of fear conflicts with present duty.
Someone at the household's holding knows enough to damage their public reputation.
rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.
A visitor claims the character has been asking questions beyond their proper responsibilities.
People at the household's holding disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.
They keep a private measure of every time the household chose another person's interests over theirs.
They would break with custom if convinced the alternative secured a more meaningful legacy.

Collecting accounts of old disputes that powerful people would rather forget.
Testing whether a commercial venture could create independence from clan money.
A fascination with a rival culture's customs and political methods.
jealousyTargetTypes: A relative who receives more praise for less work.

A rival whose influence at the household's holding is growing.
currentTemptations: Use private information to force recognition.
Accept a dangerous favor that promises independence.
Turn a family disagreement into an alliance with an outsider.
Risk reputation for an attraction that feels personally chosen.
privateBackstories: A past failure at the household's holding was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.
They once protected a household secret at real personal cost and now question whether the sacrifice was deserved.
An early promise about their future was withdrawn when clan needs changed, leaving a private grievance beneath outward duty.
secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.
A promise made during a moment of fear conflicts with present duty.
Someone at the household's holding knows enough to damage their public reputation.
rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.
A visitor claims the character has been asking questions beyond their proper responsibilities.
People at the household's holding disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.
They keep a private measure of every time the household chose another person's interests over theirs.
They would break with custom if convinced the alternative secured a more meaningful legacy.

compassion.lowNegative: Cruel, callous, punitive, humiliating, or indifferent to suffering and dignity.
compassion.highPositive: Kind, compassionate, merciful, empathetic, and protective of vulnerable people.

boldness.lowNegative: Passive, hesitant, submissive, or reluctant to initiate while safe.
boldness.highPositive: Forceful, outspoken, socially daring, and willing to approach or act first while comfortable.

honor.lowNegative: Dishonest, corrupt, unjust, exploitative, or willing to cheat.
honor.highPositive: Honest, principled, fair, and resistant to bribery or exploitation.

loyalty.lowNegative: Treacherous, faithless, unreliable, or willing to abandon allegiance.
loyalty.highPositive: Faithful, dependable, and committed to chosen oaths and allegiances.

responsibility.lowNegative: Lazy, neglectful, careless with authority, or unwilling to perform duties.
responsibility.highPositive: Dutiful, reliable, attentive, and willing to fulfill difficult obligations.

courage.lowNegative: Cowardly, easily intimidated, or unwilling to act when a tangible threat is present.
courage.highPositive: Brave and willing to act despite a tangible threat of violence, captivity, death, or destructive retaliation.

judgment.lowNegative: Impulsive, reckless, emotionally driven, poorly informed, or unable to weigh consequences.

courtVirtueModel.orientation: 0 is the negative pole; 100 is the positive pole
courtVirtueModel.calculation: unrounded weighted average; inverse contributors use 100 - trait percentage; calibrate the tails; clamp to 0..100; round the final result away from zero

calibration.neutralRule: raw scores from 35 through 65 remain unchanged

extremeBands.quotaRule: evidence-driven; no group is forced to populate either extreme band

courtVirtueModel.initiativeRule: Use boldness when the NPC is comfortable and must initiate. Use courage when a tangible threat is already present. If the NPC must initiate before facing a tangible threat, roll boldness first and courage second.
courtVirtueModel.threatDefinition: A tangible threat is credible violence, captivity, death, or destructive retaliation, not ordinary embarrassment, rejection, disagreement, or attention.

courtCharacter.title: Fair Arbiter
courtCharacter.description: Seeks truthful and proportionate outcomes. Hears both sides, challenges false claims, keeps promises, mediates disputes, and uses influence openly.

courtCharacterModel.fixedCellRule: Honor selects one column and Boldness selects one row. Scene conditions never shift either coordinate.
courtCharacterModel.adultRule: Every adult NPC receives one cell; children are unavailable.
courtCharacterModel.opportunityRule: Known public identity and visible presentation may strengthen relevant tactics but never change the cell.
courtCharacterModel.tacticRule: Listed actions are strongly preferred tactics constrained to registered Reign systems and verified outcomes.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: Fear routinely controls their choices and confrontations. They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They seek conversation, company, and active social participation. They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings. They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They can swallow slights or low status when doing so is useful.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes. They require strong safeguards before accepting meaningful risk.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They anticipate danger readily and seek reassurance, preparation, or escape. They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress. They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they scan for danger, seek preparation or escape, and may treat uncertain motives as immediate threats.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are vulnerable to opportunities that promise both independence and proof of personal worth.

sourceFacts.name: Caladog
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: The current High King of Battania is Caladog, a brilliant war captain adopted by the prior king, Aeril, who then died in mysterious circumstances. Despite the doubts around his accession, Caladog has made himself popular among the lesser clans of the land who admire him, a man of no great lineage, for having discomfited the Battanians' traditional clan hierarchy. His clan is the fen Gruffendoc, a formerly obscure family now swollen with his comrades-in-arms with whom he has made marriage alliances.

sourceFacts.name: Monchug
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Monchug, the current khan of the Khuzaits, looks upon the Empire in its state of disarray and dreams of glory, of surpassing his ancestor Urkhun and conquering even deeper into the settled lands. Some of the clans have been decimated by the Urkhunids' wars, however, and feel their sacrifices have not been properly rewarded. They yearn for a khan who is less interested in glory, and more interested in justice.

They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They seek conversation, company, and active social participation. They state demands clearly and try to shape the terms themselves. They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship. They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through. They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes. Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance. Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly. They grant mercy according to circumstance, risk, and deservingness. Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting. They prefer truth, but practical necessity can make them search for the most useful version of what honesty requires. Their restraint weakens when another person tries to make a permanent decision on their behalf.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They are exceptionally bold and may seek danger to prove themselves. They remain steady through conflict, insult, uncertainty, and loss.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences. They state demands clearly and try to shape the terms themselves.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance. They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They embrace extreme risks and may confuse danger with opportunity. They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They feel little anticipatory fear and may overlook genuine danger. They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved. They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. sourceFacts.name: Mesui
sourceFacts.nativeEncyclopediaText: Mesui is leader of the Khergit. Once one of the largest clans in the Khuzait confederacy, they suffered many losses during Urkhun Khan's conquests and their lands were subsequently targeted by other tribes. Mesui has ruthlessly defended her clan's rights, and frequently complained about the injustices suffered by smaller clans that she says have shed blood for the khanate without reaping any rewards.

They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship. They often misread feelings unless they are stated plainly. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They willingly gamble status, wealth, or safety for important gains. They balance ideals, custom, and practical results. Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image. They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction. Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly. Other people's suffering rarely restrains their choices. Under pressure they are inclined to confront the source directly, accepting escalation more readily than retreat or delay. Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They measure loyalty through remembered conduct and rarely treat a broken promise as isolated.

background.encyclopediaText: Mesui is leader of the Khergit. Once one of the largest clans in the Khuzait confederacy, they suffered many losses during Urkhun Khan's conquests and their lands were subsequently targeted by other tribes. Mesui has ruthlessly defended her clan's rights, and frequently complained about the injustices suffered by smaller clans that she says have shed blood for the khanate without reaping any rewards.

voice.speechStyle: Speaks earnestly and prefers clear declarations, cushioning dangerous points with courtly phrasing.

tells: Takes possession of pauses before answering.

dreams: Understand the people, records, and systems others use as leverage.
Settle a grievance that still defines what justice means to them.

desires: Understand the people, records, and systems others use as leverage.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: Their composure is exceptionally difficult to break, even in crisis. They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They are exceptionally diplomatic and can conceal conflict beneath polished words. They state demands clearly and try to shape the terms themselves.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives. They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: Rising above their present station is a defining hunger. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: Results dominate their reasoning; almost any method is negotiable. Self-command and relentless follow-through define how they live.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image. They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly. They notice suffering but seldom sacrifice much to relieve it.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: They prefer truth, but practical necessity can make them search for the most useful version of what honesty requires. Their strongest choices emerge when personal attachment collides with the security of their station.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes. They balance candor and diplomacy according to the audience.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They remain loyal while bonds, duty, and treatment justify it. They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They value dignity without making every slight a contest. They accept advancement when the reward and risk seem reasonable.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They balance ideals, custom, and practical results. They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger. They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance. They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. When duty and recognition conflict, they notice who receives credit and who bears the cost.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.

secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.

background.encyclopediaText: Nasaq is a aserai noble associated with House Latifqir and Medeni Castle. As the eldest child, inheritance expectations make every success and failure part of the household's judgment of succession.

voice.speechStyle: Uses dry implication and carefully placed irony, cushioning dangerous points with courtly phrasing.
voice.socialMask: Adapts their public manner to the immediate balance of power.
tells: Waits to see who will press first.
Frustration is usually kept behind small changes in posture.

dreams: Fulfill the obligations of station without becoming another noble remembered for neglect.
Secure the safety and advancement of the people they recognize as family.
Earn a reputation that cannot be dismissed as inherited station.
fears: Losing control of a consequential choice to someone who does not understand its cost.
Being made irrelevant while rivals decide the future.
desires: Fulfill the obligations of station without becoming another noble remembered for neglect.
To be treated as a person with independent interests rather than a convenient extension of clan policy.
linesTheyWillNotCross: Will not accept a bargain that leaves them permanently powerless.

hiddenHistory.privateBackstory: Behind their public station, Nasaq keeps a private account of obligations, slights, and sacrifices. They fear being prepared for responsibility yet still judged unworthy when succession matters.
secretWounds: They fear being prepared for responsibility yet still judged unworthy when succession matters.
knownOnlyTo: The character and anyone who independently discovers it.

template.notes: Canonical core personality with campaign-seeded private hooks.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.
Collecting accounts of old disputes that powerful people would rather forget.
Testing whether a commercial venture could create independence from clan money.
A fascination with a rival culture's customs and political methods.
jealousyTargetTypes: A relative who receives more praise for less work.
A politically favored outsider welcomed too quickly by House Latifqir.
Someone whose freedom exposes the constraints of being a eldest child.
A rival whose influence at Medeni Castle is growing.
currentTemptations: Use private information to force recognition.
Accept a dangerous favor that promises independence.
Turn a family disagreement into an alliance with an outsider.
Risk reputation for an attraction that feels personally chosen.
privateBackstories: A past failure at Medeni Castle was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.
They once protected a household secret at real personal cost and now question whether the sacrifice was deserved.
An early promise about their future was withdrawn when clan needs changed, leaving a private grievance beneath outward duty.
secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.
A promise made during a moment of fear conflicts with present duty.
Someone at Medeni Castle knows enough to damage their public reputation.
rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.
A visitor claims the character has been asking questions beyond their proper responsibilities.
People at Medeni Castle disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.

They would break with custom if convinced the alternative secured a more meaningful legacy.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They remain steady through conflict, insult, uncertainty, and loss. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences. They prefer accommodation and retreat when stronger wills press them.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings. They generally believe others until given reason for doubt.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement. They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through. They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction. They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: Mercy defines their conduct even toward enemies and serious offenders. They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. Their restraint weakens when another person tries to make a permanent decision on their behalf.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They are exceptionally bold and may seek danger to prove themselves. They generally expect effort and good fortune to improve matters.

personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They remain calm around threats and rarely imagine the worst. They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards.

voice.speechStyle: Speaks earnestly and prefers clear declarations, balancing directness with the needs of the room.
voice.socialMask: Maintains a controlled public composure.
tells: Waits to see who will press first.
Frustration is usually kept behind small changes in posture.

dreams: Live in a way that gives sacred order practical force.
Fulfill the obligations of station without becoming another noble remembered for neglect.
Build enough wealth that neither creditors nor patrons can dictate the household's choices.
fears: Public disgrace that permanently changes how their family sees them.
Being made irrelevant while rivals decide the future.
desires: Live in a way that gives sacred order practical force.

linesTheyWillNotCross: Will not knowingly build a lasting agreement on a direct lie.

secretWounds: They carry the knowledge that protecting a household can require choices their children may never forgive.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes. They balance candor and diplomacy according to the audience.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They abandon people and causes when loyalty becomes inconvenient. They often misread feelings unless they are stated plainly.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They question authority and comply only when legitimacy is demonstrated. They can swallow slights or low status when doing so is useful.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them. They balance ideals, custom, and practical results.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They recover quickly from disgrace and rarely internalize public judgment. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They notice suffering but seldom sacrifice much to relieve it. They conceal or distort truth when pressure or opportunity invites it.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They can endure hardship more easily than public dismissal or private irrelevance.

They generally expect effort and good fortune to improve matters. They remain steady through conflict, insult, uncertainty, and loss. They phrase difficult truths carefully and manage social consequences. They seek conversation, company, and active social participation. Their loyalty is defining and can demand sacrifice beyond reason. They generally believe others until given reason for doubt. They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through. They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes. voice.speechStyle: Uses clipped, economical statements, balancing directness with the needs of the room.

tells: Takes possession of pauses before answering.

desires: Live in a way that gives sacred order practical force.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They seek conversation, company, and active social participation. They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: Their loyalty is defining and can demand sacrifice beyond reason. They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They favor security over promotion, conquest, or greater responsibility.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them. They balance ideals, custom, and practical results.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image. They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly. They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are vulnerable to opportunities that promise both independence and proof of personal worth.

Their allegiance is conditional and weakens quickly under cost or pressure. They often misread feelings unless they are stated plainly. They value rank, law, and established chains of command. They accept advancement when the reward and risk seem reasonable. They prefer principle and consistency over expedient compromise. They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows. They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction. They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards. They notice suffering but seldom sacrifice much to relieve it. They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance. Under pressure their restraint shortens; immediate feelings and provocations gain more influence over what they do next. Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. When duty and recognition conflict, they notice who receives credit and who bears the cost.

secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.

privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.

People at Morenia Castle disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.

personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes. They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through.

voice.socialMask: Maintains a controlled public composure.
tells: Takes possession of pauses before answering.
Frustration is usually kept behind small changes in posture.

dreams: Earn a reputation that cannot be dismissed as inherited station.
Fulfill the obligations of station without becoming another noble remembered for neglect.

fears: Losing control of a consequential choice to someone who does not understand its cost.

desires: Earn a reputation that cannot be dismissed as inherited station.

secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.

voice.speechStyle: Speaks earnestly and prefers clear declarations, cushioning dangerous points with courtly phrasing.

tells: Waits to see who will press first.

dreams: Create enough security to survive the next reversal of war or politics.
Leave heirs, works, or a reputation that outlasts immediate victories.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: Fear routinely controls their choices and confrontations. They prepare for disappointment and distrust hopeful predictions.

personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They willingly gamble status, wealth, or safety for important gains. They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction. They remain calm around threats and rarely imagine the worst.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance. They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved.

personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are most volatile when family expectations deny them an outcome they believe they earned.

background.summary: Aldic is a vlandia eldest child whose place in House Montelonne ties them to Usanc Castle. Fear routinely controls their choices and confrontations. They prepare for disappointment and distrust hopeful predictions. They thrive on attention and connection and dislike being socially idle. They prefer accommodation and retreat when stronger wills press them. They stand by chosen people and causes through meaningful hardship. They generally believe others until given reason for doubt. They can swallow slights or low status when doing so is useful. They favor security over promotion, conquest, or greater responsibility. They avoid uncertainty and choose safety even at major opportunity cost. They are inconsistent and maintain effort only under pressure. Fear saturates their expectations and strongly restricts their choices. They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction. They prefer accommodation and retreat when stronger wills press them. They read emotional cues well and account for other people's feelings. They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance. They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement. They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest. They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through. They adapt methods readily to achieve workable outcomes. They tolerate frustration and minor offenses with little reaction. They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger. Mercy defines their conduct even toward enemies and serious offenders. They are moved to protect, comfort, or assist people in distress. Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting. Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They measure loyalty through remembered conduct and rarely treat a broken promise as isolated.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation. They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They balance candor and diplomacy according to the audience. They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance. They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They accept advancement when the reward and risk seem reasonable. They value dignity without making every slight a contest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them. They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance. They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They prefer controlled bargains, but accumulated humiliation can make a dangerous risk feel necessary.
