personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They are exceptionally bold and may seek danger to prove themselves. They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They state demands clearly and try to shape the terms themselves. They are reserved and engage mainly when duty requires it.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They often misread feelings unless they are stated plainly. Their allegiance is conditional and weakens quickly under cost or pressure.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They accept advancement when the reward and risk seem reasonable.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They willingly gamble status, wealth, or safety for important gains. They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction. They remain calm around threats and rarely imagine the worst.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are pitiless and see suffering as useful, deserved, or irrelevant. Other people's suffering rarely restrains their choices.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they are inclined to confront the source directly, accepting escalation more readily than retreat or delay.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are most volatile when family expectations deny them an outcome they believe they earned.

tells: Takes possession of pauses before answering.

dreams: Settle a grievance that still defines what justice means to them.
Earn a reputation that cannot be dismissed as inherited station.
Build enough wealth that neither creditors nor patrons can dictate the household's choices.
fears: Losing control of a consequential choice to someone who does not understand its cost.
Being made irrelevant while rivals decide the future.
desires: Settle a grievance that still defines what justice means to them.
To be treated as a person with independent interests rather than a convenient extension of clan policy.
linesTheyWillNotCross: Will not accept a bargain that leaves them permanently powerless.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.
Collecting accounts of old disputes that powerful people would rather forget.

jealousyTargetTypes: A relative who receives more praise for less work.

currentTemptations: Use private information to force recognition.
Accept a dangerous favor that promises independence.
Turn a family disagreement into an alliance with an outsider.
Risk reputation for an attraction that feels personally chosen.
privateBackstories: A past failure at Marunath was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.
They once protected a household secret at real personal cost and now question whether the sacrifice was deserved.
An early promise about their future was withdrawn when clan needs changed, leaving a private grievance beneath outward duty.
secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.
A promise made during a moment of fear conflicts with present duty.
Someone at Marunath knows enough to damage their public reputation.
rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.
A visitor claims the character has been asking questions beyond their proper responsibilities.
People at Marunath disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.
They keep a private measure of every time the household chose another person's interests over theirs.
They would break with custom if convinced the alternative secured a more meaningful legacy.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure. They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They state demands clearly and try to shape the terms themselves. They balance candor and diplomacy according to the audience.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They often misread feelings unless they are stated plainly. They are guarded and expect proof before relying on others.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through. They balance ideals, custom, and practical results.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: Disgrace, exposure, or moral failure weighs heavily on their self-image. They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: Truthfulness defines their self-respect, even when honesty is costly. They are pitiless and see suffering as useful, deserved, or irrelevant.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure their restraint shortens; immediate feelings and provocations gain more influence over what they do next.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They can endure hardship more easily than public dismissal or private irrelevance.

personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They are usually composed but can be shaken by serious pressure.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They balance candor and diplomacy according to the audience. They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They remain loyal while bonds, duty, and treatment justify it. They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They value dignity without making every slight a contest. They judge authority by circumstance, competence, and personal interest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They can follow plans but bend when fatigue or temptation grows. They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger. They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They grant mercy according to circumstance, risk, and deservingness. They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are vulnerable to opportunities that promise both independence and proof of personal worth.

voice.speechStyle: Speaks quietly and makes listeners lean in, balancing directness with the needs of the room.

tells: Waits to see who will press first.

dreams: Build enough wealth that neither creditors nor patrons can dictate the household's choices.
Secure the safety and advancement of the people they recognize as family.

fears: Losing control of a consequential choice to someone who does not understand its cost.

desires: Build enough wealth that neither creditors nor patrons can dictate the household's choices.

linesTheyWillNotCross: Will not accept a bargain that leaves them permanently powerless.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.
Collecting accounts of old disputes that powerful people would rather forget.

jealousyTargetTypes: A relative who receives more praise for less work.

currentTemptations: Use private information to force recognition.
Accept a dangerous favor that promises independence.
Turn a family disagreement into an alliance with an outsider.
Risk reputation for an attraction that feels personally chosen.
privateBackstories: A past failure at Lycaron was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.
They once protected a household secret at real personal cost and now question whether the sacrifice was deserved.
An early promise about their future was withdrawn when clan needs changed, leaving a private grievance beneath outward duty.
secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
Public comparison with relatives still feels like a verdict on their worth.
They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.
A promise made during a moment of fear conflicts with present duty.
Someone at Lycaron knows enough to damage their public reputation.
rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.
A visitor claims the character has been asking questions beyond their proper responsibilities.
People at Lycaron disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.
They keep a private measure of every time the household chose another person's interests over theirs.
They would break with custom if convinced the alternative secured a more meaningful legacy.

personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance. They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: Results dominate their reasoning; almost any method is negotiable. They embrace extreme risks and may confuse danger with opportunity.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They feel little anticipatory fear and may overlook genuine danger. They feel little personal shame and resist moral or social embarrassment.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are pitiless and see suffering as useful, deserved, or irrelevant. They lie readily and shape truth around advantage.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. They are most volatile when family expectations deny them an outcome they believe they earned.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.

privateBackstories: A past failure at Ortysia was quietly blamed on someone else, and the character has never decided whether relief or guilt matters more.

secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.

They remember the first time clan duty overruled a choice they believed was their own.
privateEntanglements: An unresolved favor links them to a household rival.
A discreet correspondent expects repayment for old information.

rumors: Some servants believe the character is preparing to challenge a household decision.

People at Ortysia disagree over whether recent generosity was sincere or strategic.
privateTruths: They have imagined leaving the role chosen for them.

Chagtai has a rounded temperament rather than a single governing trait. They are exceptionally bold and may seek danger to prove themselves. They remain steady through conflict, insult, uncertainty, and loss. They state demands clearly and try to shape the terms themselves. They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance. They often misread feelings unless they are stated plainly. They grant or withhold trust according to evidence and circumstance. They strongly defend their status, achievements, and self-respect. They actively seek greater status, influence, or achievement. They embrace extreme risks and may confuse danger with opportunity. They control their habits and reliably carry difficult plans through. They feel little anticipatory fear and may overlook genuine danger. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance. They are pitiless and see suffering as useful, deserved, or irrelevant. They notice suffering but seldom sacrifice much to relieve it. Under pressure they narrow their attention, contain visible emotion, and try to impose an orderly plan before acting. personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: They show ordinary courage when duty or necessity requires it. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance. They lead or yield according to status, confidence, and stakes.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives. They remain loyal while bonds, duty, and treatment justify it.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They accept advancement when the reward and risk seem reasonable. They value dignity without making every slight a contest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They prefer principle and consistency over expedient compromise. They accept measured risks when expected gains justify them.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They feel shame when failure clearly violates important standards. Their temper rises according to stress, insult, and circumstance.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved. They grant mercy according to circumstance, risk, and deservingness.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure they weigh the immediate danger against duty and self-interest, with circumstance deciding whether caution or resolve wins.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. Their strongest choices emerge when personal attachment collides with the security of their station.

personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. personalityPortrait.coreTemperament: Stress readily unsettles them and colors their decisions. They see both opportunity and danger without a fixed expectation.
personalityPortrait.socialStyle: They favor plain speech even when it embarrasses or provokes. They are comfortable alone or among others depending on circumstance.
personalityPortrait.trustAndAttachment: They remain loyal while bonds, duty, and treatment justify it. They understand familiar emotions but miss subtler or alien perspectives.
personalityPortrait.powerAndStatus: They favor security over promotion, conquest, or greater responsibility. They value dignity without making every slight a contest.
personalityPortrait.decisionStyle: They prefer principle and consistency over expedient compromise. They are inconsistent and maintain effort only under pressure.
personalityPortrait.emotionalPattern: They become annoyed quickly and show impatience under friction. They experience ordinary fear proportionate to apparent danger.
personalityPortrait.moralBoundaries: They are truthful or deceptive according to circumstance. They care when suffering is immediate, personal, or clearly undeserved.
personalityPortrait.underPressure: Under pressure their restraint shortens; immediate feelings and provocations gain more influence over what they do next.
personalityPortrait.internalContradictions: Their competing needs do not form a simple virtue or flaw; rank, danger, affection, and humiliation can pull different parts of the same personality to the surface. dreams: Fulfill the obligations of station without becoming another noble remembered for neglect.

secretInterests: Private correspondence with someone outside the expected social circle.

secretWounds: They fear affection is conditional on usefulness.
